summary: The existing canonical Stabat Mater array is an extracted first-thirteen-tercet source. The 1962 Benziger Missale has a twenty-tercet September 15 sequence; do not conflate this with the shorter Feria VI post Passion Sunday sequence or a 21-tercet anthology combining mutually exclusive stanza 19 alternatives.

source.work: Missale Romanum editio iuxta typicam, Benziger Brothers, 1962
source.passionFridayUse: The same 1962 Missale OCR places a shorter Stabat sequence in Passiontide (printed p. 501) ending after the eighteenth tercet. Keep its liturgical use distinct.

missingFromCanonical.latin:
Iuxta Crucem tecum stare,
Et me tibi sociare,
In planctu desidero.

Virgo virginum præclara,
Mihi iam non sis amara:
Fac me tecum plangere.

Fac, ut portem Christi mortem,
Passionis fac consortem,
Et plagas recolere.

Fac me plagis vulnerari,
Fac me Cruce inebriari,
Et cruore Filii.

Flammis ne urar succensus,
Per te, Virgo, sim defensus,
In die iudicii.
missingFromCanonical.qualification: September OCR appears to omit 'ne' in 'Flammis urar succensus'; March 1962 text and independent September source include 'ne'. Do not settle without image-level printed page comparison.

missingFromCanonical.latin:
Christe, cum sit hinc exire,
Da per Matrem me venire
Ad palmam victoriæ.
missingFromCanonical.qualification: Chosen on the Sept 1962 Mass sheet. The alternative 'Fac me cruce custodiri ...' is NOT an extra twenty-first stanza in this witness.

missingFromCanonical.latin:
Quando corpus morietur,
Fac, ut animæ donetur
Paradisi gloria. Amen.

historicalVariants.stanza19Alternate:
Fac me cruce custodiri,
Morte Christi præmuniri,
Confoveri gratia.
historicalVariants.policy: Mutually exclusive edition readings at stanza 19. Do not combine as 21 stanzas in the 1962 September Mass sequence.
historicalVariants.septemberStanza18OcrCaution: Printed-page proof required for 'ne' before urar. More than one OCR/transcription witness differs; avoid confident claim of exact print wording.
